text:
ravi: Quick proposal: lightweight read-only control-plane replicas living in customer VPCs (or Private deployments) to handle authz checks, cert validation, and local routing decisions. Goal: cut cross-region latency and egress charges for handshake-heavy workloads.

isabel: Interesting. Are these full control-plane copies or a reduced surface?

ravi: Reduced. They would contain: tenant config, signing certs (public keys), route table snapshots, and short-lived revocation lists. No secrets that require customer KMS. Write operations still go to canonical central CP.

toni: Main tradeoffs I see: consistency window (stale revocations), complexity of sync, and attack surface in customer VPCs. Also, audit logs need to be shipped back centrally.

sam: For consistency, can we do hybrid: CDC stream for critical events (revocations, pin/unpin) + periodic snapshot for everything else? That keeps revocation lag < 1s for critical items and snapshot TTL ~30s.

ravi: Exactly what I had in mind. CDC over encrypted gRPC stream (mutual TLS) from central CP to local replica. If CDC breaks, replica switches to snapshot polling.

isabel: How do we protect signing certs and avoid secret leakage in customer-managed environments?

ravi: We only store public material in replicas. Any private signing stays centralized or uses customer KMS/HSM via an agent. Replica verifies signatures but never holds signing keys.

toni: Onboarding complexity: operator will need to create an IPsec/Privatelink connection, create the replica resource, and set up the stream ACL. That's a lot of surface for SRE. We should automate heavily and provide templated infra.

sam: Also need a clear fallback: if replica is unhealthy, connectors should fall back to central CP gracefully with measurable SLO. How do we signal that?

ravi: Replica will expose /health with structured codes: healthy, degraded(stream-lag), stale(snapshot-age). Connector reads header `X-CP-Replica-Status` and falls back if status != healthy.

isabel: What about audit logs? Customers in Private mode may require logs stay on-prem. We should allow two modes: push logs securely to central telemetry, or write-only local storage accessible to customer auditors, with a signed periodic manifest sent to central CP for attestation.

toni: Good call. That solves regulatory constraints. Also add checksumed manifests so central CP can verify no tampering.

sam: DNS implications: connectors need to resolve replica endpoints with low TTLs. For Privatelink we'll give stable A-records, for peering we may rely on ENI. Need to ensure route preference when both local and global exist.

ravi: We'll add routing priority: prefer local CP when replica healthy and lag < threshold. Otherwise use global. Config snippet I sketched: 

```json
{
  "replica": {
    "enabled": true,
    "mode": "readonly",
    "cdc_priority": ["revocations","pin-state"],
    "snapshot_interval_s": 30,
    "max_stream_lag_ms": 1000
  }
}
```

isabel: Security: how do we bootstrap trust for the replica? We need attestation so connectors don't accept forged local replicas.

ravi: Bootstrapping flow: operator creates replica via central API -> central issues a signed replica certificate (short-lived) -> operator installs cert on replica host. Replica cert is bound to tenant ID and VPC CIDR. Replication streams use mTLS and we validate cert chain at both ends.

toni: Edge-case: split-brain if central CP believes replica is unhealthy and replica still serves. Need a decisive authoritative flag in connector handshake (central CP authoritative). Maybe connectors should force revalidation for any auth decisions older than X seconds.

sam: Tie that to a central TTL: decisions older than, say, 5s require revalidation. But that revalidation would spike traffic if many requests hit boundary; so we should probabilistically revalidate (5% per request) and ramp up if errors increase.

isabel: Observability: metrics to add: `replica_stream_lag_ms`, `replica_snapshot_age_s`, `replica_failover_count`, `replica_auth_decisions_served`. Alerts: replica_auth_decisions_served > 90% while replica_snapshot_age_s > 60s.

ravi: Ops plan: start with a single-region pilot for a set of low-sensitivity tenants in Private mode. Will require operator-run onboarding and a flag in operator to opt-in.

toni: Rollout safety: feature gated by `replica_readonly_enabled` and we should support opt-out per-tenant. Add a kill-switch in central CP to forcibly revoke replica certs.

sam: What's the storage model? Lightweight on-disk caches with WAL for incoming CDC so we can resume streams. Keep retention minimal (minutes) to reduce footprint.

ravi: Yup. Disk footprint target <100MB for a tenant. We maintain in-memory route index for fast lookups.

isabel: Tests: e2e harness that simulates network partition, verifies connectors fall back within expected SLO, and asserts no unauthorized access during partition. Also threat-modeling review.

deploy-bot: @ravi started canary rollout: cp-replica-agent -> staging (3%) at 2025-12-10T14:22:00Z.

eng-oncall: I'll add oncall runbook: steps to revoke replica cert, force connector fallback, and collect manifests for audits.

ravi: Next actions: 1) I'll draft lightweight RFC with sequence diagrams and the bootstrap + revoke flows. 2) isabel will run threat model and compliance check. 3) toni will prototype operator onboarding scripts. 4) sam will sketch tests and fallback SLO.

isabel: Sounds good. Please include sample log lines and the manifest format in the RFC.
avi: Will do. Thanks y'all :rocket:
